# DSR-0.1: Official defer and resume protocol

Status: Research recorded. Scope decisions remain open.

Read date: 2026-09-30 America/Denver (2026-10-01 03:52 UTC). This record covers DSR-0.1 only. No engine execution or real model check was performed.

## Official evidence

Source H: [Hooks reference, Defer a tool call for later](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later). The browser fetch succeeded. Its v2.1.246 requirement concerns plan mode resume, not general defer support.

Verbatim excerpt from the resume instruction: “The same tool call fires `PreToolUse` again.”

Protocol summary: in `claude -p`, defer preserves the call and exits with `tool_deferred`. The caller reads `deferred_tool_use`, collects input, and resumes with the same permission host. In the documented `AskUserQuestion` round trip, the hook allows with `updatedInput`; the tool executes. This example does not establish that every tool requires `updatedInput`. Repeat defer while waiting is permitted. Later defer ignored after allow: **not stated**.

Limits: batches ignore defer and follow normal permission evaluation; unavailable tools produce `tool_deferred_unavailable` before the hook. Cleanup applies. Interactive mode ignores defer. With `-p`, reapply nondefault permission options. Host supplied `tool_result` injection is undocumented here.

Source S: [Agent SDK hooks, Outputs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks#outputs). The old platform domain redirects here. This source confirms that defer ends the query, `updatedInput` is ignored with defer, and precedence is deny, defer, ask, allow. It points to Source H for resume instructions. It provides no host supplied result protocol in the material reviewed.

## Classification and consequences

Exactly one ticket outcome applies: **the official text documents only the path where the hook fires again and answers allow**.

A-01 has a documented answer to the documentation question, but its runtime assumption is not retired. A-01 concerns synthetic result acceptance. The read establishes that this mechanism remains undocumented in these sources; it does not establish that the mechanism fails. DSR-1.3 still owns proof with a real model.

A2 now has primary documentation support for its resume sequence. That does not make A2 primary in this design. The design requires effects to execute in effect Activities, while A2 permits the resumed engine to execute the tool. Adopting A2 therefore needs a deliberate change to the guarantee or a new mechanism to preserve it. That is an operator decision for DSR-0.2 and a document change for DSR-0.3, neither made here.

Proposed next action: prepare OI-1 option b, the request to document host supplied results. The operator owns the decision to send it. No contact or external message was sent. Pending that decision, retain the synthetic path as the existing proposed primary mechanism, subject to DSR-1.3 proof and explicit dependency risk.

The batch limit conflicts with treating the design's fake model observations as a general engine contract. DSR-1.3 should test batches on the selected engine before any batch safety promise is accepted. This is a proposed test implication, not a change to the spec or ticket scope.

## Version and evidence limits

- Official minimum engine version for general defer: not stated in the reviewed section.
- Official documentation publication date: not stated in the reviewed material. The read date above is not a publication date.
- Runtime version tested by this ticket: none. The spec's prior fake model observation names Claude Code 2.1.285; this record does not reverify it or assign current documentation to that version.
- Full verbatim protocol acceptance criterion: partially met. This record contains a short exact excerpt and a precise source section, rather than reproducing the full protocol. The web source quotation limit permits no more than 25 words from Source H. A reviewer can compare the summary against the numbered protocol at the link. The excerpt is 7 words.
- Unreachable section acceptance criterion: not applicable because the section was reached. The earlier EV-57 failure remains historical evidence, not the current result.
- Later defer after allow acceptance criterion: met by the explicit **not stated** finding. Repeat defer before an eventual allow does not prove defer after that allow.

The URLs and source titles above are the supporting citations. Browser extraction line locators observed for review were H: 1749-1775 and S: 357-367, 455; these locators are transient and are not stable document identifiers.
